original.paper_title: Top Score on the Wrong Exam: On Benchmarking in Machine Learning for Vulnerability Detection

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: The prevailing function-level binary classification definition of ML4VD is ill-defined because vulnerability often cannot be decided without calling context.
claims.evidence_quote: the vulnerability of a function cannot be decided without further context for more than 90% of functions

claims.statement: Popular ML4VD datasets contain noisy labels: only 39%-65% of sampled functions labeled vulnerable actually contain security vulnerabilities.
claims.evidence_quote: Out of the 100 functions per dataset that were originally labeled as vulnerable, only 39%-65% actually contain security vulnerabilities.

claims.statement: High ML4VD benchmark scores can be achieved via spurious correlations without detecting vulnerabilities.
claims.evidence_quote: high scores can be achieved even when only word counts are available

metrics.name: context_dependent_vulnerability_ratio
metrics.setting: manual labeling of 300 vulnerable-labeled functions from BigVul, Devign, DiverseVul
metrics.evidence_quote: the vulnerability of a function cannot be decided without further context for more than 90% of functions

metrics.name: noisy_label_ratio
metrics.evidence_quote: only 39%-65% (Devign: 47%, BigVul: 39%, DiverseVul: 65%) actually contain security vulnerabilities

metrics.name: inter_rater_agreement
metrics.setting: first labeling step: vulnerable vs secure
metrics.evidence_quote: the labels of the two researchers agreed for 82% of all functions

metrics.name: cohen_kappa
metrics.setting: first labeling step: vulnerable vs secure
metrics.evidence_quote: resulting in a Cohen Kappa value of 0.64

metrics.name: inter_rater_agreement
metrics.evidence_quote: the labels of the two researchers agreed for 98% of all functions

metrics.name: cohen_kappa
metrics.evidence_quote: resulting in a Cohen Kappa value of 0.96

original.overall_conclusion: The paper argues that function-level binary classification is an ill-defined task for ML4VD because vulnerability labels depend heavily on context and many labels are noisy. Popular datasets can be exploited via spurious correlations, so reported high scores do not demonstrate real vulnerability detection capability.
original.comparable_notes: Fair comparisons should account for dataset noise, use patch-commit/CVE-confirmed labels, and report whether vulnerability is context-dependent versus context-independent. Evaluations should not rely solely on function-level classification accuracy without addressing spurious correlations.
